messages:
maya: heads up — after the state transfer to the new s3 backend (infra-state-prod-gpu) last night, applies for the eu-south-2 gpu pools are failing with a dynamodb lock mismatch. provisioning CI started erroring and nodes are stuck in Pending.
samir: ugh, can you paste the exact error from terraform apply? any lock id shown?
maya: short snippet below:

```
Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed

  on backend.tf line 0:
  in data "terraform_remote_state":
  ...

Lock Info: LockID: 9c8f3a2e-... owner: 1234567890
```

maya: it looks like the lock id baked into the old state doesn't match the item we see in the new Dynamo table after the move. we moved the state file and the lock table reference points to the previous key.
samir: did you move the Dynamo table or just the S3 bucket/object? mixing backends is risky.
maya: just moved S3 key and updated backend config to a new account s3://infra-state-prod-gpu, same dynamodb table name but in a cross-account table. thinking the lock item TTL raced out during the copy.
luke: any CI runs that were mid-apply during the copy? that would create a stale lock.
emily: oncall-bot reported 3 failed applies in eu-south-2 around 02:14 UTC, looks like the last apply had a partial write on the lock item.
infra-bot: Automated alert: 3 failed terraform applies detected for module.gpu_pool in eu-south-2 between 02:10-02:20 UTC. See run ids: gh-actions/8743, gh-actions/8751.
samir: ok first rule: do NOT force-unlock unless we're coordinated. If there's an active apply it's dangerous.
maya: agreed. i inspected the table with: `aws dynamodb get-item --table-name terraform-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"9c8f3a2e-..."}}'` and saw the holder set to the old account id and a nonzero TTL still present.
luke: possible fix path: 1) confirm no active chef/automation running, 2) run `terraform force-unlock 9c8f3a2e-...` from the account that owns the lock, 3) re-run apply. alternatively revert backend to the old bucket/key until we can migrate safely.
emily: to avoid repeating: we should disable CI for gpu pools in eu-south-2 while we coordinate a manual unlock and a controlled state import.
maya: i'm going to pause CI and revert the backend config in the repo to point at the previous s3 key (infra-state-prod-gpu-legacy) so ongoing pipelines don't stomp on it. will notify.
samir: while CI is paused, we can either: A) remove the lock item from Dynamo (if TTL expired and no active apply) using aws cli delete-item, or B) run force-unlock from the previous account's creds. i'd prefer force-unlock + audit so we have a record.
emily: i'll own disabling the pipeline and annotating the run. tagging @luke to coordinate the unlock window.
luke: i'll SSH into the ops bastion and run the force-unlock after we confirm no applies. command: `terraform force-unlock 9c8f3a2e-...` from terraform v1.4.6 w/ backend pointing at legacy bucket. i'll post output here.
maya: thanks. also adding a small doc to PREVENT future drift: when moving state between accounts, copy both S3 object and Dynamo lock item export/import and coordinate 5m maintenance window.
oncall-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-0048 "state transfer race -> gpu provisioning impact". Pinned to eng-infra channel.
luke: ran force-unlock, output: `Unlock successful for LockID 9c8f3a2e-...`
re-ran terraform apply in a canary namespace and it completed. then gradually re-enabled CI.
maya: confirmed nodes provisioning resumed and GPU CI jobs started passing. rolling apply across the rest of the pool is in progress, no more lock errors seen.
samir: nice. follow-ups: 1) add a small terraform migration playbook to PR checklist, 2) add Automation to pause CI when backend changes detected, 3) include lock export step when moving state.
emily: created a short runbook PR and added the incident note with steps and links to the AWS CLI commands we used. cc @security for cross-account handling.
maya: closing the thread — thanks everyone :thumbsup:
